note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason: cinatra#2932 (lifecycle-b W5a) — the LENT ACTION reaches the card's OWN decision path, and that is the whole point of the slice rather than an accident of it. The plan's rule is "using the action is pressing the button. Same identity, same permissions, same recorded decision", and the epic's structural rule is ONE implementation per interaction — so the new self-MCP primitive (src/lib/lifecycle/lent-action-mcp.ts) calls `submitReviewDecisionAction` and `approveReviewTaskInternal`, the same entries the review page and the gate-scoped decide route call, instead of a second decision implementation. Registering it on the shared MCP module list puts that path's module graph onto the four MCP-reachable locked routes: +38 modules (the decision path's graph). The remaining +6 on those routes (and the +1 on /sign-in) are the slice's own six leaves — the bound-reference resolver, the bound-turn actor, the bound-card binding, the grant codec, its single-use store and the store's DDL leaf — reached from `runAssistantTurn`, which mints the grant at send time. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: re-implementing the decision inside the primitive (a second place where 'approved' can come to mean something different — the one-card rule forbids it), and deferring the decision modules behind a dynamic import (measured: no change, the analyser counts a dynamic edge exactly like a static one, so it would have bought nothing and hidden the dependency from the reader). MEASURED AS A DELTA on two trees analysed identically by scripts/route-graph.mjs with the companion extension fleet ABSENT ON BOTH — origin/main at e37f68d630c5d69c107deef997902634fc1e3f3c and this branch's head — so the same first-party imports are unresolved in each and the DIFFERENCE between the two counts is exact even though the absolute counts are deflated: 1212 -> 1250. `from` is therefore not re-measured here; it is main's own ceiling, measured in CI with the fleet cloned pinned. The carried-forward #2939 / #2928 records for these routes are RETIRED BY THIS RAISE, which is the one lifecycle the gate allows for an annotation whose ceiling moves.
